title: feat: support `podman [container|pod] clone` for remote connection
body:
### Feature request description

The `podman [container|pod] clone` does not work for remote connections

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/bbf98ecfcc041fafa143da08fb0fed9da0b82020/pkg/domain/infra/tunnel/containers.go#L1082-L1084

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/bbf98ecfcc041fafa143da08fb0fed9da0b82020/pkg/domain/infra/tunnel/pods.go#L206-L208

The e2e are disabling it when dealing with remote 

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/bbf98ecfcc041fafa143da08fb0fed9da0b82020/test/e2e/pod_clone_test.go#L17

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/bbf98ecfcc041fafa143da08fb0fed9da0b82020/test/e2e/container_clone_test.go#L17

### Suggest potential solution

Implement the clone feature for remote connections

### Have you considered any alternatives?

In Podman Desktop we implemented our own "cloning" feature, where we inspect the container config, to rebuild it.

### Additional context

- https://github.com/redhat-developer/podman-desktop-hummingbird-ext/issues/408

comments.body: @axel7083 thanks for the issue.  I'm curious what your intent is given that podman desktop has worked around this.  Are you simply hoping that we enable this for remote connections and you guys would then remove yours or do you have something else in mind?

> Are you simply hoping that we enable this for remote connections and you guys would then remove yours or do you have something else in mind?

Yes this is exactly what I would be hopping for :D 

Recently, we noticed that our implementation was lacking some config, our implementation was not cloning the port binding. This remind me that podman has already such feature, and I never took the time to open the issue, so today was the day!

any interest in contributing? it would be more than a little effort in the sense that it would require an API endpoint and tests, bindings, tunnel plumbing and tests (e2e and bats).  

i dont think any of this is particularly hard ...

> 8\. any interest in contributing? it would be more than a little effort in the sense that it would require an API endpoint and tests, bindings, tunnel plumbing and tests (e2e and bats).
>         i dont think any of this is particularly hard ...

Yes sure!

out of curiosity, i asked claude what it would need to do to enable this, and it did get most of it correct.  But then I asked what it's confidence of work it would, and it said it was moderate to low. (which i thought was funny).  Anyways, it clearly admits it doesnt understand our swagger stuff (who does?) and was very concerned about writing and verifying the tests.
would you like this assigned to you?

Just for the record I am somewhat sure that the podman implementation also has gaps, the internal architecture makes cloning extremely fragile so I would not be surprised if several less used option get lost that way as well.

I have no objections to adding remote support here, local support exists already but personally I would generally avoid any kind of workflow relying on clone at all. As part of Podman Desktop that is not a choice you make, you just expose existing functionality so thats fine.
Users should really have some kind of declarative config, be it a quadlet file, compose, kube yaml or just a stored podman run command. There should not be a case where users do not know how they created the container and need to "clone" IMO.

@Luap99 is correct here about the work flow.  I wasn't very specific here but that was kind of why I was poking around about why you needed it.  anyways, if the workflow is deemed valid, i suppose theoretically you could just enable to the API portion of this and not further expose more commands to the cli.  that would mean PD would interact soley with the restful api.  i dont know if we have precedent here, but i would think the team would entertain thought (or at least a conversation about it).

>  i suppose theoretically you could just enable to the API portion of this and not further expose more commands to the cli. that would mean PD would interact soley with the restful api. i dont know if we have precedent here, but i would think the team would entertain thought (or at least a conversation about it).

Well if we have local support than we should have podman-remote support unless there is a major reason why this is not useful or possible.
UI wise it is just always confusing why some things only work on linux, at least in cases where the remote client is marketed as the "podman" such as windows and macos.

Just to give some context on how we use our implementation of the cloning feature today. For the [Hummingbird](https://hummingbird-project.io/docs/using/overview/) project, we created a dedicated extension [podman-desktop-hummingbird-ext](https://github.com/redhat-developer/podman-desktop-hummingbird-ext). This extension have a few features, but it mainly offer the users èalternativeè images, it detects for example docker images, and offer you to "clone" your existing containers and replace the base image with an Hummingbird alternative. The workflow try to offer you to seamlessly clone and restart your container while you keep the same config.
